name: Huitzilopochtli

domain_history.domain: minor tribal/patron deity in early Mexica tradition
elevated to co-equal imperial patron-deity status with Tlaloc, Tezcatlipoca, and Quetzalcoatl, associated with war and the sun, as the Mexica state's "chosen people" war-and-sacrifice ideology

notes: Patron deity of Tenochtitlan. Political instrumentalization: Tlacaelel, who held the cihuacoatl office (chief counselor/co-ruler) under several successive Mexica tlatoque across roughly six decades (d. 1487), is credited by multiple sources with this mid-15th-century theological reorganization — sourced with moderate-high confidence, since the causal Tlacaelel-reform narrative rests on somewhat thinner/later secondary sourcing than the archaeological/textual facts it explains. Birth myth (the Coatepec narrative — Coatlicue miraculously impregnated, decapitates/dismembers her daughter Coyolxauhqui via the newborn Huitzilopochtli) is textually attested in Sahagún's Florentine Codex, Book 3 (1575-1577, post-conquest); the Coyolxauhqui monolith (Templo Mayor excavations) provides independent pre-conquest archaeological corroboration of the myth's antiquity in sculptural form.
